findings.description: This bucket is declared with no ACL restriction and no accompanying aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block / bucket policy, and the in-code comment states 'bucket is public'. Anonymous or cross-account principals can therefore list and read objects, and the bucket holds a customer master spreadsheet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption and without customer-managed key control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so future ACLs or bucket policies can grant public access with no account-level guardrail preventing it.
Server access logging is not configured (the comment confirms it), so reads and writes to a bucket holding customer data leave no audit trail for detecting exfiltration.

A file named customer-master.xlsx is uploaded from the repository into the public, unencrypted 'data' bucket with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument, exposing sensitive customer records both at rest and to anonymous readers. The source file is also committed to version control.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so financial records are stored without enforced encryption or customer-managed key control.
The bucket relies solely on a 'private' ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving no guardrail against a later policy or ACL change exposing financial data publicly.
Server access logging is not configured for a bucket holding financial data, so there is no audit record of object access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so stored objects are not protected by enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing prevents a subsequent ACL or bucket policy from making the bucket publicly readable.
Server access logging is not enabled, leaving no audit trail of access to the bucket's objects.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the 'private' ACL is the only barrier to public exposure and can be overridden by a later policy change.
The centralised log bucket uses a 'log-delivery-write' ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing prevents accidental public exposure of the audit logs it aggregates.
